name: Accident and Emergency
description: Receives walk-in and ambulance patients, triages them Red, Amber or Green, and treats or refers them.

name: Acute and General Medicine
description: Admits patients from A&E who need hospital care for more than a few hours: infections, breathing problems and frailty.

name: Cardiology
description: Diagnoses and treats heart conditions such as heart attack, heart failure and arrhythmias.

name: Gynaecology
description: Cares for conditions of the female reproductive system, including early pregnancy emergencies.

name: Neurology
description: Assesses and treats conditions of the brain and nerves, including stroke and epilepsy.

name: Gastroenterology
description: Investigates and treats conditions of the digestive system, liver and pancreas.

name: Radiology
description: X-rays and CT scans, done by radiographers and reported by radiologists.

name: Operating Theatres
description: Operating theatres where surgeons do emergency operations.

name: Pharmacy
description: Supplies the hospital's medicines and prepares medicines for patients to take home.

name: Trauma and Orthopaedics
description: Treats broken bones and joint injuries, from plaster casts to hip operations.

name: General Surgery
description: Operates on emergencies of the abdomen such as appendicitis, gallbladder problems, blocked bowels and hernias, and cares for them before and after theatre.

name: Critical Care (ICU/HDU)
description: Intensive care and high dependency beds for the sickest patients: from Resus, after big operations, and ward patients who get worse.

name: Maternity
description: Midwives deliver babies on the labour ward, mothers and babies recover together on the mother and baby ward, poorly newborns go to the neonatal unit, and pregnant women come for antenatal appointments and scans. Women in labour come straight here, not to A&E.

name: Outpatients
description: Reception and waiting for booked clinic appointments. Every clinic's patients check in here.

name: Facilities
description: Cafes and vending machines for patients and visitors, run by outside contractors who pay the hospital a share of the takings.
